lines.t: This guy robbed two banks without a mask. His disguise? Lemon juice. On his face.
A friend told him the secret. Lemon juice is invisible ink. So if it's on your face, cameras can't see you.
Sounds dumb. So he tests it. Juice on the face. One instant photo.
The photo comes out... and his face isn't there!
Proof! Probably he just aimed the camera at the ceiling. But proof.
So he walks into a bank. No mask. Looks straight into the security camera.
Takes the money. Walks out. Easy.
Then a second bank. Same face. Same camera. Still invisible... he thinks.
Months later, his face is on the eleven o'clock news. Crystal clear.
The phones at the police station start ringing.
Less than an hour later, police knock on his door.
They show him the tape, and he is shocked.
You see, he wasn't lying. He really believed it. He didn't know enough to know he was wrong.
And here's the twist. A psychology professor read about him in the newspaper... and started testing students on jokes, grammar and logic.
The worst scorers were sure they were above average. The less people know, the more confident they are.
Today it has a name. The Dunning-Kruger effect.
So the robber who thought he was invisible... became famous in every psychology class.
Would you trust that photo? A, yes. Or B, test it twice.
